top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) offers the most distinctive voice on the slate together with sustained imaginative architecture. On public knowledge, the Blinding (Orbitor) cycle and Solenoid build memory, the body, dream and cosmology into one project, in dense, rhythmic Romanian prose with a poetic imagination at its base. I would anchor the citation in the prose project and name poetry only as its foundation, since translation coverage of the poetry is thin. The main unresolved risk is whether the late volumes deepen the architecture or only re-run its obsessions. Translation may also flatten the sentence-level voice. I cannot settle either point without close reading, and I have not read or independently verified any text. Carson (P002) is second. Her formal renewal across genres is a serious standard of sustained achievement, and a citation resting on the core books (the verse novel, the elegy and the essay-poems) answers my doubt about her consistency across smaller projects. Tawada (P003) is third on the strength of her bilingual method, though I cannot judge her Japanese and German corpus in full. P000 is last because the shortlist contains several writers of real literary achievement. Adonis has no proposal in the slate and so cannot be ranked.
recusal_note: None apparent from the supplied profile, which records no personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted writer. My own Central European documentary fiction and long residence in Prague and Vienna are context only, not evidence of a preference. As disclosed in round 2, a Central European sensibility could incline me toward a Romanian writer, and I have tried to weigh the case on the stated criteria.
